title: Cold Reply
tagline: Two meanings: a short, distant answer in a chat, or a prospect's first response to cold outreach.
excerpt: In chat, a short and distant answer like "ok". In sales, a prospect's first reply to an email or message they never asked for.
definition: In a text or chat, a cold reply is a short, distant answer such as "ok", "k" or "fine" that shows little warmth or interest. In sales, a cold reply is a prospect's first response to a cold email or LinkedIn message they never asked for, whether it is interested, a brush-off or a question.

sections.heading: Cold reply in chat
paragraphs: A cold reply in chat is short and flat, and it closes the conversation instead of opening it: "ok", "k", "hmm", "fine" or a single emoji, often after a long gap. It can feel like disinterest, but one short message rarely means much on its own. People answer briefly when they are busy, tired or on their phone.

A pattern of cold replies over several days is the real signal. The best response is to match their length, ask one easy, open question, and give them space. If the replies stay cold, it is fair to ask directly or step back.

sections.heading: Cold reply in sales
paragraphs: In B2B sales, "cold" describes the relationship, not the tone. A cold reply comes from a prospect who had no prior contact with you and never asked for your [cold email](/resources/glossary/cold-email) or LinkedIn message. It can be friendly, curt or a question, and it marks the moment cold outreach becomes a real conversation.

A cold reply is not a yes. Across Myntmore-managed campaigns, 1% to 3% of prospects reply, and at least 20% of those replies are positive. How fast and how well you answer decides whether the reply turns into a meeting: our guide to [handling cold email replies](/resources/blogs/handling-cold-email-replies) covers the four replies you will get and what to say to each.

rows.label: Typical wording
cells: "send me more info", "not right now", "who else do you work with?"

rows.label: What it usually means
cells: Busy, distracted or not very interested
Some curiosity, a polite exit, or a request for proof

rows.label: How to respond
cells: Match their length, ask one open question, give them space
Answer within an hour with one short, specific question, not a deck

sections.heading: Cold reply vs. warm reply
paragraphs: A warm reply comes from someone who already knows you or asked to hear from you, so you can move straight to a call. A cold reply comes from someone who owes you nothing and is deciding in seconds whether you are worth another message. Keep the answer short, specific and easy to say yes to. See also [warm lead](/resources/glossary/warm-lead).

faqs.question: What does cold reply mean?
faqs.answer: It has two meanings. In everyday chat, a cold reply is a short, distant answer such as "ok" or "k" that shows little warmth or interest. In sales, a cold reply is a prospect's response to a cold email or message they never asked for, which signals some interest or a question, not a decision.

faqs.question: How should I respond to a cold reply in chat?
faqs.answer: Don't read too much into one short message, since people reply briefly when they are busy. Match their length, ask one easy open question, and give them room. If every reply is cold over several days, that is the real signal, and it is fair to ask directly or step back.

faqs.question: Is a cold reply a bad sign in sales?
faqs.answer: No. In sales, cold only means the prospect had no prior relationship with you. Any reply means your message was read and answered, which most cold outreach never gets. Even "send me more info" or "not right now" is an opening. Answer quickly with one short, specific question rather than a pitch or a deck.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a cold reply and a warm reply?
faqs.answer: A cold reply comes from someone with no prior relationship who never asked to hear from you. A warm reply comes from someone who already knows you or asked for contact. Warm replies can move straight to a call. Cold replies need a short, specific answer that earns the next message, not a pitch.
